task.description: WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup) for ISS-0106. This issue is EXPLICITLY a recurrence class: decision record 0005-pin-formatting-toolchain.md was written because `mix format --check-formatted` had already failed twice for the same underlying cause (ISS-0008/GH#12 and ISS-0068/GH#229), and 0005's own REVIEWER sign-off chose the pin that ISS-0106 now reports as unenforced. So Step 0.5's job here is not merely 'is there a prior match' -- there certainly is -- but to establish the full recurrence history and, specifically, WHY the previously-chosen fix did not hold. Read every prior formatting/toolchain-drift issue record in docs/issues/ (at minimum ISS-0008 and ISS-0068; grep the directory for 'format', 'formatter', 'tool-versions', 'toolchain', 'warnings-as-errors' to find any others, including any filed by other hosts since) and 0005 in full. Per WF-03 Step 0.5 rule 2, a recurring root cause is flagged at MAJOR or above regardless of the original severity. Do NOT diagnose or fix anything in this step -- Step 1 is the diagnosis and it is your next handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Every prior issue record describing formatter drift or toolchain-version mismatch is listed by id with its status, its resolution method, and the toolchain version it was resolved under (quote the actual line from each record; do not summarise from memory)
The search that produced that list is stated as an actual command with its actual output, not asserted -- so that 'no others exist' is a measured result rather than an inferred absence
States explicitly whether ISS-0106 is a recurrence of the same root cause as the prior records, with the evidence for that judgement

States what the previously-applied fix was in each case and identifies specifically why it did not prevent this occurrence (the key question: 0005 DECIDED a pin -- determine from git history whether the pin was ever actually applied, i.e. when .tool-versions was added, by which commit/run, and whether the follow-on application task 0005 names ever ran)
Severity re-assessed and stated, with WF-03 Step 0.5 rule 2 applied explicitly
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step

result.summary:
VERDICT: ISS-0106 IS a recurrence -- the FOURTH occurrence of the formatter-drift class and the SECOND occurrence of the struct-update-warning class. Critically, the finding that contradicts this handoff's own leading hypothesis: decision 0005's chosen fix WAS applied. It was not skipped.

SEARCH ACTUALLY RUN (AC2). `grep -ril -e format -e formatter -e tool-versions -e toolchain -e warnings-as-errors docs/issues/` aborted (exit 134) under this shell, so the search was re-run via ripgrep, case-insensitive, over all 105 files in docs/issues/. A first pass on the bare word 'format' returned 32 files -- too broad, because 'format' matches ordinary prose. The narrowed pattern `check-formatted|mix format|tool-versions|toolchain|warnings-as-errors` (rg -i, content mode, no head limit) returned matching lines in exactly these 17 files: ISS-0008, ISS-0012, ISS-0015, ISS-0016, ISS-0019, ISS-0020, ISS-0030, ISS-0035, ISS-0036, ISS-0040, ISS-0041, ISS-0044, ISS-0046, ISS-0053, ISS-0057, ISS-0068, ISS-0069, ISS-0070, ISS-0074, ISS-0086, ISS-0087, ISS-0106, ISS-0107. Most of those are incidental mentions ('verified: mix format --check-formatted clean') in unrelated records. Reading each, the ones that actually DESCRIBE formatter drift or toolchain-version mismatch as the defect are the five listed below. 'No others exist' is therefore a measured result over the full directory, not an inferred absence.

PRIOR RECORDS, quoted (AC1):

1. ISS-0008 -- severity BLOCKER, status resolved, resolved_at 2026-08-15T19:59:00Z. Title line 2: 'mix format --check-formatted fails on pre-existing files under Elixir 1.20.3 (formatter paren-style drift vs. project's declared ~> 1.14)'. Resolution method, line 60-62: 'Resolved via option (a): ran real `mix format` (not --check) on exactly the 5 affected files under this environment's actual toolchain (Elixir/Mix 1.20.3, OTP 29).' Toolchain resolved under: Elixir/Mix 1.20.3, OTP 29. Line 63-64 explicitly declined the pin: 'mix.exs's `elixir: "~> 1.14"` constraint left as-is'. Same record also added .gitattributes eol=lf (a separate CRLF-vs-formatter cause, not the version-drift cause).

2. ISS-0068 -- severity BLOCKER, status resolved, resolved_in_run WF03-ISS0068-20260819, resolved_at 2026-08-19T05:31:28Z. Title lines 2-5: 'mix format --check-formatted fails on 14 pre-existing committed files under Elixir 1.18.3/Mix 1.18.3 (OTP 27) -- formatter paren/line-break drift, same class as ISS-0008'. Resolution method, lines 63-65: 'Recommended action taken this run: reformat the 14 files under this host's toolchain (mix format, no other changes) so this host's gate is unblocked now, per Unblock-Everything.' Toolchain resolved under: Elixir 1.18.3 / Mix 1.18.3 / OTP 27. Lines 45-47 already named this run's exact failure mode in advance: 'whichever host commits last "wins" formatting-wise and silently un-formats every other host's next `mix format --check-formatted` run.' Lines 65-72 are what produced decision record 0005.

3. ISS-0035 -- severity MINOR, status resolved, resolved_in_run WF03-ISS0035-20260817, resolved_at 2026-08-17T19:56:00Z. Title line 2: 'test/letflow/definitions/promotion_digest_test.exs fails mix format --check-formatted'. Resolution method, lines 37-39: 'Ran `mix format` repo-wide rather than scoping to just the one named file, because a fresh `mix format --check-formatted` (run to confirm the fix) surfaced a second, previously-undetected drift'. Toolchain resolved under: NOT RECORDED -- the record names no Elixir version anywhere; it attributes the drift to line length ('4 lines exceeding the configured line length', line 22-23) rather than to a version difference, and predates the pin. Included here because it is the same gate failing on files the discovering run did not touch, and because the record's own inability to name its toolchain is itself evidence for AC6's 'the records do not settle it'.

4. ISS-0046 -- severity MAJOR, status resolved, resolved_in_run WF03-ISS0046-20260818, resolved_at 2026-08-18T08:41:51Z. Title line 2: 'mix compile --warnings-as-errors fails on lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex -- struct-update type-inference gap in dispatch_start/4, dispatch_end/3, dispatch_human_task/3'. This is ISS-0106's Symptom 2, in one of the same files. Line 20: '`mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29) fails with three type warnings, all "a struct for Letflow.Engine.InstanceState is expected on struct update"' -- verbatim the same warning text ISS-0106 reports. Resolution method, lines 82-84: 'added explicit struct pattern matches (%InstanceState{} = instance_state, %Token{} = token, as applicable per function) to the 3 affected private functions' own parameter lists'. Toolchain resolved under: Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29. Line 44-47 flagged the version question and left it open: 'Whether this is new in Elixir 1.20 specifically (vs. already present under whatever toolchain version REQ-044/049 were originally verified against) is UNCONFIRMED -- this environment only has 1.20.3 available to check against; no older Elixir install was reachable to compare.' That UNCONFIRMED is the exact question ISS-0106's Step 1 AC3 now has to settle, and the Docker route makes it settleable for the first time.

5. ISS-0016 -- severity MINOR, status resolved, resolved_at 2026-08-17T07:29:19Z. Title line 2: '.formatter.exs excludes priv/repo/migrations/** and lacks import_deps: [:ecto_sql], so no migration file has ever been format-checked by the project gate'. Adjacent, not the same root cause: it is about the formatter's INPUT SCOPE, not about version drift. Listed for completeness because it is why .formatter.exs today carries the `import_deps: [:ecto_sql]` that Step 1's container run has to satisfy. Toolchain: not recorded. ISS-0012 (MINOR, resolved 2026-08-17T07:49:27Z) is likewise adjacent-only -- it is README staleness ABOUT ISS-0008, not a drift occurrence.

IS THIS A RECURRENCE, AND ON WHAT EVIDENCE (AC3): YES, on both symptoms, and the evidence is textual identity rather than resemblance. Symptom 1 is the same command (`mix format --check-formatted`) failing on the same class of file (pre-existing, untouched by the discovering run) for the same stated cause (Mix's formatter heuristics differ between Elixir releases) as ISS-0008 and ISS-0068 -- and it is the specific third occurrence 0005 predicted in writing: 0005 line 32, 'A third occurrence should be expected under the status quo.' Symptom 2 is the same warning string ('a struct for X is expected on struct update') in a set of files that INCLUDES lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, the single file ISS-0046 was filed and resolved against. Note the direction of travel is opposite between the two recurrences of Symptom 1: ISS-0008 failed under 1.20.3 on files written under an older formatter; ISS-0068 failed under 1.18.3 on files written under a newer one; ISS-0106 fails under 1.20.3 again. That oscillation is itself the signature of unenforced-pin drift rather than of any one host being wrong.

WHAT THE PRIOR FIX WAS AND WHY IT DID NOT HOLD (AC4) -- and this is the part that corrects the handoff's framing. The handoff asks whether the pin was ever actually applied. It was. Measured from git history, not inferred:
  `git log --diff-filter=A --format='%H %ad %an %s' --date=iso-strict -- .tool-versions` returns exactly one commit: 68edfbcf61936c2c3dfe4028f1b8cc600d114222, 2026-08-19T10:56:34+05:00, Vladimir Titenko, 'Apply Decision 0005: pin Elixir/OTP toolchain (#234)'. `git log --oneline --all -- .tool-versions` returns that same single commit and no other -- the file has never been modified since it was added.
  `git show --stat 68edfbc` shows the follow-on task 0005 names did run, and did MORE than 0005's minimum: .tool-versions (+2, 'elixir 1.18.3-otp-27' / 'erlang 27.2'), mix.exs (elixir: '~> 1.14' -> '~> 1.18'), README.md (+13/-4, Notes section rewritten to point at the pin), and lib/letflow/design/decision0005-toolchain-pin-apply.md (+87). Its commit message states 'mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, and mix test all pass clean (5 properties, 1029 tests, 0 failures)' and cites 'queue task 126, GH#233'. So: the decision was made, the follow-on task was filed, the follow-on task ran, and it was verified green at the time.
  THEREFORE the reason the fix did not prevent this occurrence is NOT non-application. It is that every mechanism 68edfbc added is DECLARATIVE and none is EXECUTIVE:
  (i) .tool-versions is inert unless a version manager reads it. 0005's own con column said so (lines 47-51: 'this repo has no CI ... it would rely on every host's own `mix letflow.check` run'), and the applying commit's own message admits asdf was absent even on the applying host: 'asdf is not installed on this host, so `asdf list-all erlang` could not be run to confirm the exact installable patch string.' A pin file applied by a host with no version manager, onto a fleet with no guarantee of one, selects nothing.
  (ii) The mix.exs backstop was written weaker than intended and weaker than the README claims. 68edfbc set `elixir: "~> 1.18"`. In Elixir's version syntax `~> 1.18` means >= 1.18.0 and < 2.0.0 -- it admits 1.19, 1.20, 1.21. It does NOT restrict to 1.18.x; `~> 1.18.0` would have. README's text added by the same commit asserts the opposite -- 'it accepts any 1.18.x patch' -- and ISS-0106 line 37-38 repeats that assertion. This host's Elixir 1.20.3 therefore satisfies mix.exs cleanly and the compile-time backstop never fires. Step 1 must re-measure mix.exs's current literal value (AC5 already requires it); flagging it here because it changes what Step 1 is looking for from 'a missing backstop' to 'a present backstop with an off-by-one-component operator'.
  (iii) 0005 explicitly declined to add CI as a second layer (lines 100-102, 'What this record does not decide ... Whether to add CI'), so no enforcement point outside the developer's own shell exists at all.
  Net: 0005 chose option (a) over (c) precisely because (c) 'has already been tried twice with the same result each time' -- but the applied form of (a) retains (c)'s enforcement profile, because the selecting mechanism (a version manager) was never established on any host. What 0005 bought was a documented target to drift back toward, which is exactly and only what its own line 50-51 predicted it would buy.

SEVERITY RE-ASSESSMENT, WF-03 Step 0.5 rule 2 APPLIED EXPLICITLY (AC5). Rule 2: 'If it's recurring, flag severity as at least MAJOR regardless of the original severity.' This is recurring (established above on two independent symptom classes), so MAJOR is the floor. ISS-0106 is filed at MAJOR, so the floor is already met and no downgrade is permissible. Recommending ORCH consider elevation to BLOCKER, with the evidence rather than the decision: both prior occurrences of this exact class were filed at BLOCKER (ISS-0008 line 6, ISS-0068 line 9); the impact statement that justified BLOCKER for ISS-0068 (lines 57-61: `mix letflow.check` is GIT_MERGE.md's Step Final gate and 'checks the *whole* file tree, not a diff -- so this blocks Step Final for every WF-02/WF-03 run dispatched from this host until fixed, regardless of what that run's own change touches') applies verbatim to ISS-0106 on this host today; and this occurrence carries an aggravating factor neither predecessor had -- a decision record already exists, was already signed off, and was already applied, so the normal remedy has been exhausted. I am not editing docs/issues/ISS-0106.yaml's severity field: AC6 forbids modifying files outside handoffs/ in this step, and the elevation is ORCH's to record.

NO FILES OUTSIDE handoffs/ MODIFIED (AC6): this step ran only read and search operations (Read, ripgrep, git log, git show). `git status --short` shows no tracked source file touched by it.

issues.description: ISS-0106 is a recurrence (4th of the formatter-drift class after ISS-0008/ISS-0068/ISS-0035; 2nd of the struct-update-warning class after ISS-0046, in an overlapping file set that includes lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex). WF-03 Step 0.5 rule 2 sets a MAJOR floor, already met by the issue's filed severity. Elevation to BLOCKER is recommended for ORCH's decision, on the evidence that both prior occurrences of this exact class were BLOCKER and that the standard remedy (a signed-off decision record, applied) has already been exhausted.

Decision 0005's fix WAS applied -- commit 68edfbc, 2026-08-19, the only commit ever to touch .tool-versions. The recurrence is not a dropped follow-on task; it is that all three mechanisms 68edfbc added are declarative and none selects or rejects a toolchain at execution time: .tool-versions needs a version manager no host is confirmed to have (the applying host provably did not), mix.exs was tightened only to '~> 1.18' which admits 1.20.x, and 0005 explicitly deferred CI. Any fix design that re-applies or re-states the pin without adding an executive check will produce a fifth occurrence.

README.md (text added by 68edfbc) and ISS-0106's own description both assert that mix.exs's `elixir: "~> 1.18"` requirement 'accepts any 1.18.x'. Elixir's ~> operator on a two-component version means >= 1.18.0 and < 2.0.0, so it also accepts 1.19 and 1.20. The stated rationale for why the backstop cannot catch this drift is correct in conclusion but wrong in mechanism, and the wrong mechanism understates how weak the backstop is. Step 1 re-measures the literal value under AC5; the doc correction belongs to whichever run implements the fix.

ISS-0046 (resolved 2026-08-18) left the version-attribution of the struct-update warnings explicitly UNCONFIRMED because no older Elixir install was reachable to compare against. Step 1's container route makes that comparison possible for the first time; AC3's answer therefore also retroactively settles ISS-0046's open question and should be written so it can be cited there.

Instruction-precedence conflict reported per core-directives.md: this handoff's task.description states as background that 0005's 'follow-on application task' may never have run and directs the step to determine 'whether the pin was ever actually applied'. Git history shows it was (68edfbc). Following the handoff's acceptance criterion (which asks the question empirically) rather than its framing (which presumes the answer). Recording it so the framing is not inherited by a later run.
